items.title: The Anti-AI ETF Is Here, and Its Biggest Holdings Are Engines, Trucks and Air Conditioners
items.summary: A new ETF built on diesel engines, truck fleets, and air conditioners is pitching itself as a refuge from software-heavy portfolios, but its biggest holding may already be cashing in on the very trend it claims to avoid.

items.title: What Are Wall Street Analysts' Target Price for Lennox Stock?
items.summary: Lennox has significantly underperformed the broader market amid weaker residential demand and reduced guidance, while analysts remain moderately optimistic about its prospects.

items.title: 2 Reasons to Like LII (and 1 Not So Much)
items.summary: Over the last six months, Lennox’s shares have sunk to $437.64, producing a disappointing 17.3% loss - a stark contrast to the S&P 500’s 10.9% gain. This might have investors contemplating their next move.

items.title: 2 Industrials Stocks to Research Further and 1 We Avoid
items.summary: Industrials businesses quietly power the physical things we depend on, from cars and homes to e-commerce infrastructure. But they are at the whim of volatile macroeconomic factors that influence capital spending (like interest rates), and the industry has underperformed the market over the past six months as its 1.3% return lagged the S&P 500 by 9.7 percentage points.

items.summary: Residential weakness offset by commercial growth; recovery pushed to 2027.

items.title: MOD Q1 Earnings Top Estimates on Data Center Growth, Sales Miss
items.summary: Modine's fiscal Q1 earnings beat estimates as data center sales surge 90%. However, revenues miss, and supply-chain pressure squeezes margins.

items.title: Lennox International (LII) Is Down 22.4% After Cutting 2026 EPS Guidance Amid Residential Weakness – Has The Bull Case Changed?
items.summary: Lennox International recently reported its second-quarter 2026 results, showing modest sales growth to US$1,545.3 million but slightly lower net income of US$269 million, while also trimming full-year earnings guidance to US$23.00–US$24.00 per share. Beneath the headline numbers, a 24% revenue increase in the commercial Building Climate Solutions segment contrasted sharply with a 7% residential decline, underlining how shifting demand between non-residential projects and pressured homeowners...

items.title: LII Q2 Deep Dive: Residential Weakness and Guidance Cut Overshadow Commercial Gains
items.summary: Climate control solutions innovator Lennox International (NYSE:LII) missed Wall Street’s revenue expectations in Q2 CY2026 as sales rose 3% year on year to $1.55 billion. Its GAAP profit of $7.73 per share was in line with analysts’ consensus estimates.
